doc.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
title: Leading his own New York group, booked by Basie's office
summary: He led a swinging quintet for about six years with Basie's office as manager.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When did you start with that band, start putting it together?
I think it was around 1955, 56, or something like that. I had it for about six years.
Had you settled in Los Angeles by then or were you still based in New York?

No, I maintained an apartment in New York on 372 Central Park West. I maintained a apartment there for years until I gave it up. And I stayed out here for three or four years, then I went back to New York. Then I came back here, that’s when I started doing studio work.

Before we get into the studio period, I just wanted to ask, this was your first real extended period as a bandleader. How did you handle that? How did you feel about now you were doing all the stuff that had been done for you in the past, it was all on your shoulders.

Well, I had a manager. Basie’s office was booking me. So I didn’t have that problem to look for work. We were making all the spots that all the other bands were making. We came out here to California and played the Cloister Club, we played in Las Vegas in the lounge at the Thunderbird, we played Pep’s Showbar in Philadelphia. Birdland, we were there all the time. We went all over the States, wherever there was a club.
